---
title: "Bootstrap an Existing Repository"
doc-type: how-to
---

Use this guide to add selected defaults without treating user-owned files as generated assets. Existing-repository workflows are audit-first, preview-first, and additive by default.

## 1. Get Advice

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar advise --path /path/to/repo
```

Use `--intent` when the planned work is known, such as `significant-refactor`, `prompt-migration`, `production-maintenance`, `security-review`, or `docs-setup`.

## 2. Audit The Target

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar audit --path /path/to/repo
```

Scope the audit with repeated `--asset-group` flags when only part of the repository is under consideration. The report distinguishes missing, present, and conflicting paths and states the comparison basis and selected scope.

If user-owned files conflict with generated paths, inspect read-only suggestions first:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar resolve-conflicts --path /path/to/repo
```

## 3. Preview The Narrowest Change

Preview a full selected bootstrap:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar bootstrap-existing --path /path/to/repo
```

Prefer a targeted command when one asset family is enough:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-memory --path /path/to/repo --memory-profile memory-local
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill session-focus
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-docs --path /path/to/repo
```

Use [Profiles and Skills](../reference/profiles-and-skills.qmd) to discover all profile families and selectors. Do not use `--force` during first adoption unless replacing a reviewed conflict is the explicit goal.

## 4. Apply The Reviewed Plan

Re-run the same selection with `--apply` only after the preview matches the intended ownership boundary:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar bootstrap-existing --path /path/to/repo --apply
```

Targeted commands follow the same contract:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-memory --path /path/to/repo --memory-profile memory-local --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-skill --path /path/to/repo --skill session-focus --apply
uv run python -m repo_familiar add-docs --path /path/to/repo --apply
```

Bootstrap Metadata records only written assets. Skipped conflicts are reported but not claimed as generated.

## 5. Verify And Maintain

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar check --path /path/to/repo
uv run python -m repo_familiar diff-upstream-candidate --path /path/to/repo
uv run python -m repo_familiar upgrade --path /path/to/repo --asset-group skills --preview
```

`check` reports both recorded generated assets and adopted Managed Surface assets against their checksum baselines.

Run skill refresh apply from a clean downstream worktree. Unchanged vendored skills and missing support files are eligible; locally modified or removed-reference skills remain untouched.

## Adopt Or Promote A Surface

Plain Quarto documentation alone does not prove a Static Quarto Application. When an existing implementation matches a known Managed Surface, preview `attach`; use `--accept-current` only after reviewing a manual baseline. Attachment records metadata and does not rewrite the surface.

For template evolution, preview with `migrate-template`, then use `promote-surface` or all-or-nothing `promote-template`. Missing files may be created, but edits, conflicts, extra managed assets, and manual-review strategies block the transaction. See [ADR 0010](../project-record/adr/0010-metadata-v2-preview-first-refresh.md) and the [Python-First Project Plan](../project-record/python-first-project-plan.qmd).

Use [Bootstrap Lifecycle](../reference/bootstrap-lifecycle.qmd) as the exact write and ownership contract.
